programmes.d: Police instituted an intense search when the mother of two young children went missing. Twenty years after her body was found, new technology recontextualized old evidence and pointed directly to the killer.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
In 1997, Kelly Eckart's car was found, with her belongings still in it, after she worked a late shift in Franklin, Indiana. Days later, her body was found in an isolated ravine.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.

In 1993, young mother Tammy Tatum was sexually assaulted and murdered in her Longmont, Colorado apartment. Police initially suspected her estranged husband, but did not have enough evidence to charge him and the case went cold.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.
In 1996, 54-year-old Gayle Isleib was ambushed in her Manchester, Connecticut driveway and shot to death. Police had to determine whether obsessive love was the motive for her murder.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.

It was one of the most unusual cases in forensic history. Investigators had to find a way to solve a murder case using only a squashed tomato found at the crime scene and tiny, pinpoint reflections of light in a photograph.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.
In 1985, Julie Estes was kidnapped from the Southside convenience store where she worked. Her body was found the next day, but the killing went unsolved until 2003.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.
The driver said he couldn't have hit and killed a pedestrian on a Harrisburg street. The Jeep Grand Cherokee he was leasing around that time had been sold months ago to a buyer in another state.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body.

The woman was dead. The man had been shot four times and survived. When the man's version of events contradicted physical evidence, investigators turned to forensic science to paint a clearer picture of the crime.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas. Later, a fourth murder from the same time period provided the police with far more than they realized.
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.

In 2007, Brian and Beverly Mauck were found dead in their Graham, Washington home. Using a bloody palm print and shoe prints at the scene, investigators focus their attention on Daniel Tavares, who had previously inked a tattoo on Brian's back.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun.
Flu-like symptoms of a mother and her children prove to be something more serious: thallium poisoning. After the mother's death, investigators turn their attention to finding the killer.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box. A forensic entomologist analyzes nearby insect activity to determine when the victim was killed.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.

When a wealthy real estate tycoon goes missing, it appears to be foul play. In his will, he leaves instructions in case he should die under violent circumstances — which were carried out after a hiker comes across his bullet-ridden skull.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.

Bombings are difficult to solve because the perpetrator isn't usually at the scene and the evidence goes up in smoke. In this case, pieces of plastic the size of grains of sand hold the key to finding a murderer.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers.
A police officer accused of killing his estranged wife insists she committed suicide. Investigators say it was murder — that it was physically impossible for the woman to have shot herself.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.

Investigators sift through the ashes of a fire which killed a 40-year-old woman. The fire appears to have been started by an unattended cigarette. On closer look, forensic scientists discover the cause was far more complicated.
An examination of the 2002 DC area shooting spree that resulted in ten murders.
A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial.

Investigators are baffled after finding a murder scene devoid of any physical evidence, but they suspect that the victim's dog had witnessed the crime. If so, forensic scientists would have to find some way to learn what the dog had seen.
Notepad points to kidnapper.
A family vacation turns into a nightmare when a woman is found face-down in a lake.
Debate over cause of death.
Soon after becoming pregnant by Dr. Maynard Muntzing, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates. Eventually, she raises suspicions that Muntzing is doing her harm.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.

Edward Honaker was convicted of rape, sodomy and aggravated sexual battery and sentenced to three life terms in prison. He maintained his innocence. After years in prison and writing countless letters, he finally found someone who believed him.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.
A highway patrolman was dispatched to what he thought would be a routine traffic accident — until he looked in the car. He had seen hundreds of accidents, but none with as much blood as this.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later.
Lives changed in the 20 years following an unsolved murder, and so did forensic science. In time, a high-powered microscope and DNA profiling revealed a clue no one had seen before.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.

Several suspects and conflicting evidence complicated a brutal murder investigation. But the forensics were clear on one thing: the killer knew his victim, and that alone gave investigators a head start.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.

There was no clear reason for a young, healthy college student to be dead. But when the coroner discovered a tiny clue during the autopsy, investigators were able to uncover a mystery filled with betrayal and revenge.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.

A woman is found dead in a ravine, and crucial evidence has been washed away by severe thunderstorms. Twice, the trail turns cold. Almost 20 years later, an old hat and a chip of stainless steel brings the killer to justice.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.

When police find the body of 11-year-old Krista Harrison, there are few clues to the killer's identity. But authorities are intrigued by unusual orange fibers embedded in clothing found near the victim.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.

In 1971, John List left a note with the bodies of his mother, wife and three children in his mansion ballroom before disappearing completely. Detectives must solve the case, despite having only an outdated photograph of List.
A pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom.
Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon in April 2002 after he planned to end their relationship.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a murder crime scene.

When Joann Katrinak is found dead in a corn field with her infant son, the obvious suspect is the husband and father of the victims. But insects found on the bodies reveal a vital clue which uncovers a twisted story of passion gone wrong.
A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has an almost perfect alibi.
After shooting his victims in the head, the killer staged the scene, placed the incriminating evidence into a plastic bag and tossed it into the river.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.

When a wealthy socialite died after falling down the stairs, witness accounts contradicted evidence. To find out what really happened, investigators employed a physicist and an expert in accident reconstruction.
Police use forensic evidence to re-examine the motives of a man who shot an intruder.

When a young woman disappeared, police feared she was the latest victim in a string of similar crimes. A pair of bloody gloves, unique tire tracks and ordinary pine needles provided investigators with some extraordinary clues.
A police officer accused of killing his estranged wife insists she committed suicide.
In 2004, nursing student Tamika Huston went missing from her Spartanburg, South Carolina home. A tip led detectives to her car, where they found an unknown house key that could help solve the case.
In 1988, the body of a young woman was discovered in an Ohio river.
Crystal Faye Todd's case is examined; the popular high school student was raped and murdered.
When an off-duty policeman was shot dead, his fellow officers were determined to solve the crime. They needed clues to find the killer and they discovered them in tiny fibres and an asthma inhaler.
Police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife.

Police are led on a wild goose chase when the wife of a prominent banker is kidnapped. An entomologist's unexpected discovery leads to a new suspect — and the realization that ordinary office equipment can leave extraordinary clues.
More than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984.

In 1988, when a patient dies unexpectedly in the office of California neurologist Richard Boggs, police begin what they think will be a routine investigation. Soon they uncover a bizarre story of corpse stealing, fake identity and sexual perversion.
A woman is found dead from a gunshot wound and police suspect her husband.

Janice Johnson was found dead at the foot of her basement stairs. Police in Nova Scotia had to unravel the circumstances surrounding Janice's death and answer the question: Was it an accident or murder?
In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with $500,000 in gold coins.
A man dies in his home after a long history of heart disease. A few weeks after the funeral, rumors surface that the death was no accident.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
On Halloween night 2004, Adriane Insogna and Leslie Mazzara were brutally murdered in their Napa, California home.
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box.

A woman is shot to death in her store just one day before she is to testify against the man accused of robbing her. The robber becomes the prime suspect, but he has a solid alibi: a timestamped videotape of his activities on the day of the murder.
A victim's knowledge of forensic evidence leads police to her abductor.

In an affluent suburb of Philadelphia, police were called to the scene of what appeared to be an accidental drowning. The investigation gradually focused on one suspect who had more than a million reasons to want the victim dead.
The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage.
When Washington, DC is plagued by a series of arson fires — each started with the same type of incendiary device — it's up to forensic scientists to find the clues that lay in the ashes.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.

In 2000, construction manager Darrell North was found dead in his work trailer in Ft. Worth, Texas. When investigators arrived, they found that he had been stabbed 46 times, indicating a personal relationship between the victim and the attacker.
Forensic developments reveal new facts in the case of a man convicted of sexual assault.

When the decomposed body of a teenage girl is discovered, police have no clues to her identity. To solve the case, investigators turn to bug larvae found on the body and a tiny wad of chewing gum found near the victim's body.
The murder of a couple puzzles investigators until the victims' dog leads police to the killer.
In this episode, the decade-old murder of a young Texas housewife is investigated.
Soon after becoming pregnant, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates.

6-year-old Nicole Rae Walker was killed in a hit-and-run in her Ft. Lauderdale neighborhood. The prosecutor combines the talents of an accident reconstruction expert with a video specialist to create a graphic demonstration of the moment of impact.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas.
In 1981, New York correctional officer Donna Payant disappeared and was later found in a landfill. The medical examiner not only identified the cause of death, but also found an important clue.
An abandoned, still-running car leads investigators to a body with unusual marks.

An investigation of a pediatrician, prompted by the mysterious death of one of her patients, leads to a Texas hospital where the pediatric mortality rate is higher than at any hospital in the country.
Police uncover deleted computer files during an investigation.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers. An investigator reveals that their ill health is due to mold in their modern home.
A suspicious neighbor gives police a break in a cold case.
